 Can employees add annual leave to paid public holidays?
 Ajanta Paul November 14, 2026
 Add on Google 
 UAE public sector employees will receive a three-day Eid Al Etihad holiday from December 2 to 4, while private sector workers get two days.
 Government employees can enjoy a nine-day break by taking just two days of annual leave around the National Day holiday.
 Private sector workers can secure a five-day break by using only one annual leave day on December 4.
 Employees in both sectors require employer approval for annual leave and have no automatic right to choose their leave dates.
 Under Federal Decree Law No 33 of 2021, "public holidays that fall during annual leave are usually counted as part of that leave, unless the employment contract or company policy provides better terms."
 The Eid Al Etihad holidays have been announced in the UAE for workers in the public and private sectors. Residents could enjoy an extended break of up to nine or five days, depending on their sector, using only one or two days of annual leave. 
 Government employees will have a three-day holiday from December 2 to December 4, while private sector workers will get a two-day paid break on December 2 and 3 for Eid Al Etihad, also known as National Day. 
 How employees can extend holidays 
 Depending on work schedules and sectors, residents can turn the last public holiday of the year into a longer break without using many annual leave days. 
 UAE confirms Eid Al Etihad holidays for private sector employees
 Read More Arrow Government employees could extend their three-day official holiday to nine days by taking annual leave on Monday, November 30, and Tuesday, December 1. 
 Combined with the weekends before and after the holiday, it would give employees a break from Saturday, November 28 to Sunday, December 6. 
 Private sector employees can also make the most of the midweek break by taking one annual leave day on Friday, December 4. 
 Combined with the official holiday and the weekend, they could then be away from work from Wednesday, December 2, to Sunday, December 6. 
 Law on combining public holidays with leave 
 Private sector employees can request annual leave before or after public holidays if their employer agrees. Employees do not have an automatic right to take annual leave. Employers can schedule or approve leave according to operational requirements. 
 Under Federal Decree Law No 33 of 2021, public holidays that fall during annual leave are usually counted as part of that leave, unless the employment contract or company policy provides better terms. 
 Federal government employees are covered by a separate law: Federal Decree Law No 49 of 2022. 
 Employees can take annual leave consecutively or in separate periods, as long as their line manager approves it. Public holidays and weekends are usually not included in the annual leave calculation. 
 In both the private and public sectors, employees need approval for their leave dates and cannot choose them freely.
